principles.name: a-quotation-is-not-a-claim
principles.decision: a count inside a quoted run is being discussed, and only an asserted count is checked against the pin

title: Stop the count check flagging a guide that quotes a stale figure on purpose
description:
The count rule failed the build on toron docs/guides/daemon-ops, line 73, which says: the guide index's older "40 tools" is exactly the drift the gate is for. The guide is explaining what drift looks like and quoting the old number to do it. A regex cannot tell a quotation from a claim, so the check was wrong and the documentation was right.

toron needs no change. Its index already says 38 tools, matching the pin and the emitted catalog. The drift the guide describes was fixed earlier; the guide was left describing it, correctly.

The rule now strips code spans and quoted runs, straight and curly, before comparing a number against the pin. Everything outside a quotation is still an assertion and must match. A deliberately wrong assertion in a hand-written page is still caught, proven by a negative test.

chiebukuro is the other half. Its cli-reference and guides index both claimed 23 MCP tools, split 16 knowledge and 7 memory, and the real surface is 24 tools, 17 and 7. That number was wrong in published documentation and the site faithfully projected the error. The owning repository fixed it in bd-a8p and the projection was re-synced, which changed exactly one page.

title: Move the site toolchain to bun, oxlint, and oxfmt
description:
Replace pnpm 11.21.0 + ESLint 9.39.5 with bun 1.4.2, oxlint 1.85.0 (type-aware, via oxlint-tsgolint), and oxfmt 0.70.0. Record the decision in ADR-0008 and amend ADR-0002 D6 for the three stack rows it does not cover.

oxlint coverage was measured against the outgoing eslint --print-config (86 rules) rather than assumed: all 16 react-hooks rules including the React Compiler set, and 21 nextjs rules mapping onto eslint-config-next's 22 @next/next rules. Four rules are off with the reason inline in .oxlintrc.jsonc: react-in-jsx-scope (462 obsolete hits under the React 19 automatic runtime), require-array-sort-compare (the gate scripts sort by code unit on purpose and that ordering feeds the canonical content hash, so a locale comparator would break the catalog pin), unbound-method (proxy.ts destructures closures), and prefer-tag-over-role (the ownership table is a div grid with valid ARIA roles and a responsive 2-column collapse).

Two real breakages were found and fixed rather than worked around. oxfmt reformatted the 44 hash-locked guide projections, which failed the freshness gate; content/docs/guides/** is now excluded. And check-freshness.mjs parsed app/sitemap.ts, lib/shared.ts, and next.config.mjs with single-quote-only regexes, so oxfmt's quote change silently emptied a fail-closed gate; all three are now quote-agnostic and the gate self-test still fires.

packages/tokens/theme.css opens with @import tailwindcss but the package never declared tailwindcss, which pnpm's hoisted root happened to satisfy and bun's layout did not. The dependency is now declared at 4.3.3.

Removed lucide-react and zod as unreferenced. mermaid-isomorphic was audited and KEPT: it has no source import but ADR-0002 D6 names it in the build-time-mermaid decision.

title: Add the chiebukuro walkthrough to the site docs
description:
Add a chiebukuro walkthrough to the site docs: chiebukuro is the only one of the four planes with no docs presence (ADR-0003 D3/D4, ADR-0004 D6).

Shape follows ADR-0004 D6: outcome first, numbered one-action steps, a runnable command per step, the literal output the command produces, a failure mode per step, and the durable artifact at the end.

Everything is verified against the real binary rather than written from memory. Every command in the new guide is checked by apps/toron-dev/scripts/check-guides.mjs against `chie --help` (fail-closed), and every shown output block was captured from an actual run on this host: chie status, chie qmd search, chie get, chie remember, chie memory record, chie memory recall, chie memory status.

Binding: apps/toron-dev/content/docs/guides/meta.json gains the page, guides/index.mdx gains its card.

Verify: node apps/toron-dev/scripts/check-guides.mjs (green), then the production build, then the deployed route returns 200.

principles.name: repository-is-the-only-writer
principles.decision: a guide is written in the product repository, and a copy edited on the site fails the build

title: Publish the product repositories' guides on the site instead of linking away
description:
The plane section pages listed all 44 canonical guides and pointed every row at the product repository, so the largest body of technical writing in the project was not on the site, was not in llms.txt, was not reachable over MCP, and could not be read without leaving.

scripts/sync-guides.mjs projects each docs/guides/*.mdx into content/docs/guides/<plane>/, excluding each repo's own index.mdx. catalog/guides.lock.json records two hashes per guide: the upstream bytes and the rendered page, plus the name of the transform.

The copy is not byte-identical and does not claim to be. The product guides are plain Markdown and this site compiles MDX. Six use < or { as ordinary punctuation and one has a description containing a colon-space, which is invalid YAML. One named transform, mdx-safe-v1, escapes those outside code and quotes the ambiguous scalar, and touches nothing else. Round-tripping the transform over all 44 pages reproduces the upstream files byte for byte.

The copies are committed rather than generated at build time because Vercel has no product clone and chiebukuro has no public repository to fetch one from.

ADR-0006 supersedes the ADR-0003 D4 clause that said guide bodies are never projected. The section pages now link inward, keep the canonical repository path in their own column, and describe the transform honestly rather than claiming a byte-for-byte copy.

comments.author: QuietHarbor
comments.text:
BYPASS — gate: toron strict commit guard, bead-hunk attribution rule (bd-9mb8), implemented in toron-cli/src/robot.rs via bead_hunk_violations over staged_added_lines_in.

Reason: the rule requires every bd-* token ADDED by the staged diff to appear in the commit message, so that a commit touching bead-tagged hunks names the bead. This commit adds 44 guide pages projected from four OTHER repositories, and those guides contain example bead ids inside bash command fences, for example a mail send whose thread argument is a sample bead id. Those tokens are illustrative strings from another project's documentation. They are not work items in this ledger, and naming them in this commit message would assert that this commit performs work for beads owned by other repositories, which is false.

Authorized by the operator in session on 2026-09-26, in direct response to being shown the rule, its source, and the offending token classes.

The token list is deliberately not restated here. It is recomputable at any time by diffing the staged additions for bd-* tokens, and writing it into a committed file would re-trip the same guard, which is the failure mode already documented in the receipt for torondev-docs-freshness-gate-e8t.

This is a recurring condition, not a one-off. Every future sync of scripts/sync-guides.mjs re-adds these tokens, so this bypass will be needed on every guide sync until the guard learns to exempt declared projected paths. A bead is filed in the toron repository for that change. The site already carries the analogous exemption for its own count rule, where projected pages are skipped by one named condition rather than a general skip.

title: Add the docs freshness gate for catalog pins and canonical guide sources
description:
Fail the build when the site's committed catalogs drift from the product surface, or when a canonical guide the walkthroughs project moves or retitles.

The site is stale right now, which is the point of the gate: catalog/toron-mcp.json carries 19 CLI commands while `toron catalog` emits 29 (ack-sla, agent, channel, job, presence, react, receipt, role, wait, watch), the file is generated_at 2026-08-14 / toron_version 1.1.0 while the product is 1.5.0, and 30 of 38 tool bodies differ. sync-catalogs.sh would refresh it, but nothing was failing, so the site served a stale reference page.

The gate has two halves, because they run in different places:

1. In-repo, fail-closed, runs everywhere including the Vercel build: every catalog in catalog/ is pinned in catalog/pins.json by count and by a canonical content hash, an unpinned catalog file fails, a hash mismatch fails, hand-written pages may not claim a tool, resource, or command count that is not a pinned number, and every entry in content/docs/guides/canonical.json must point at a site page that exists.
2. Upstream, best effort with a loud skip: when the product repo clone or the product binary is reachable (locally it is, on Vercel it is not), the committed catalog is compared against the live surface and a difference fails with a named diff plus the fix command. Canonical guide entries are checked against the clone for existence and frontmatter title.

Wiring: check-freshness.mjs joins prebuild, predev, and the Vercel buildCommand, so the deploy fails too. Evidence to record: gate red on today's stale catalog, catalog synced and pins re-set, gate green in both local and Vercel-like (no upstream, no binary) modes, check-guides and build and lint green, and the deployed site still 200.

comments.author: QuietHarbor
comments.text:
BYPASS: toron pre-commit guard, unattributed_bead_tokens, one incident, authorized by the operator.

Gate: toron.dev commit guard (strict). Blocked tokens: bd-mcp-inbox-assignment-tags-sdi1, bd-dup-assign-collapse-ws21, bd-slot-visibility-gv17, and 5 further bd-* ids added by the same refresh.

Why the gate is wrong for this commit: every token arrives inside catalog/toron-mcp.json, which is a generated artifact copied verbatim from toron/docs/catalog/toron-mcp.json by scripts/sync-catalogs.sh. The toron extractor appends the implementing bead id to schema field descriptions (fetch_inbox.thread_id carries bd-harvest-thread-filter-yp9r, and 7 more). The commit makes no claim about that work, the ids are not mine, and ADR-0002 D4 forbids hand-editing the catalog to remove them. Attribution cannot be honestly satisfied by reserving a reason I do not own.

Operator authorization, verbatim from the operator in session on 2026-09-26: "Authorize a recorded bypass and ship now" (chosen over fixing the toron extractor first, and over shipping the gate against the old catalog). Scope: this one commit only. The record exists before the gated action, per P5.

Accepted consequence, on the record: toron.dev is public, so the generated schema descriptions render 10 internal bead ids on the public reference pages (3 were already published by the previously committed catalog, the refresh adds 8 more). A bead for the upstream extractor fix is the follow-up, not a precondition for this commit.

principles.name: motion-conveys-meaning
principles.decision: a state is legible from how it moves, and movement that carries no meaning is decoration that costs frames

title: Give the site a motion system, compositor-only hovers, and spatial language in the crash cycle
description:
A diagnosis of the motion system, from measuring it rather than from taste.

1. No motion system exists. Six transition rules use two durations, 0.15s and 0.18s, and one easing, ease, chosen ad hoc. There is no token and no scale. A second number appearing next to the first is how a third appears.

2. Every transition animates a paint property. Five of the six animate border-color, background-color, or color, and not one animates transform or opacity. On a site whose whole visual language is a hairline border on near-black, every hover repaints the element on every frame.

3. The crash cycle has no spatial language. All four states are stacked in one grid cell and cross-faded on opacity alone, so a crash, a restart, and a resume are visually identical events that differ only in their text. The site best idea, a crash is a transition and not a lost run, is enacted with the weakest motion vocabulary available.

4. The loop is ungated and the event decays. The cycle is a 12s infinite animation with no visibility gate, so it runs off screen, and a reader still on the page sees the crash for the thirtieth time, at which point it is wallpaper rather than an event.

The fix is four moves. A duration scale and an easing vocabulary as tokens in packages/tokens, shared by marketing and docs. Hover states that cross-fade an overlay on opacity alone, so the compositor does the work and the paint properties stop animating. Each crash-cycle state given a distinct transform, so the motion tells you which state you are in before you read the word. And a play-state gate driven by an IntersectionObserver, so an off-screen loop costs nothing and does not decay a reader attention.

principles.name: canonical-origin-single-source
principles.decision: the origin is one constant, and a URL that does not serve the site may never appear in metadata

title: Serve the docs to agents as Markdown and fix the site origin
description:
Two defects and one missing contract.

1. The site advertises https://toron.dev as its origin in metadataBase, JSON-LD, openGraph, the sitemap, and robots.txt. That domain serves a different product (Sel, a Mac screen-sharing app) and is not attached to the Vercel project. Every canonical link and every sitemap entry currently points off-site at an unrelated app. The site actually serves at https://toronmail.vercel.app.

2. Every docs page renders a Copy page button and a View as Markdown popover pointing at /llms.mdx/docs/<slug>/content.md. That route does not exist, so both controls 404 on every page. /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt are also absent.

3. The Fumadocs llms integration is not wired: no docsLlms renderer, no llms.txt route, no llms-full.txt route, no /docs/<slug>.md rewrite.

This adds the llms routes, an MCP endpoint at /api/mcp with search and page tools, and a single siteUrl constant that every origin reference reads. The sitemap stops hand-listing docs URLs and derives them from the docs source tree.

title: Add per-plane docs sections covering every canonical guide
description:
The docs have one shared walkthrough shelf and a toron-only reference, so three of the four planes have no home in the docs tree and the fourth has one page. The stack has 44 canonical guides (toron 13, flywheel 19, beads 6, chiebukuro 6) and the site lists 4.

This adds one docs section per plane, each carrying the ownership line from ADR-0003 D2, the site walkthrough for that plane, and a table of every canonical guide in that plane's repository with its read-when and its canonical path. Per ADR-0003 D4 the site lists and links, it never duplicates the manual, and the canonical text stays in the product repo.

The gate is what makes "every guide" true rather than aspirational: content/docs/planes.json declares the four planes, and check-freshness.mjs fails when a plane page is missing from the docs nav, when a guide in the repo is not listed on its plane page, when a listed guide is gone upstream, or when a listed title no longer matches the repo frontmatter. Guide bodies stay unprojected, and that goes on the declared not-checked list.

Wiring: the docs root meta.json order becomes index, how-it-works, guides, then the four planes, then tools and reference, and generate-tool-docs.mjs pins that order so regeneration keeps it.

Verify: check-freshness exit 0 with the four planes checked, a negative test per plane (unlisted guide, deleted guide, retitled guide), check-guides exit 0, build exit 0 with the four routes prerendered, lint 0 problems, and the four routes 200 in production.

title: Redesign toron.dev to Linear-grade marketing + high-fidelity walkthrough docs
description:
Rebuild the toron.dev public site to the design and marketing language of linear.app and itsaplan.dev, and replace the schema-dump docs with high-fidelity walkthroughs.

Scope:
1. ADR-0004 amends ADR-0001 D2 (palette), D4 (hero), D10 (feature visualization), D12/D13, and sets a walkthrough standard for docs. ADR-0001 D2 currently LOCKS the violet palette; this is the authorising change.
2. packages/tokens: new palette (near-black canvas + indigo accent), --toron-violet renamed --toron-accent, Linear-grade type scale and radii.
3. apps/toron-dev global.css: new layout grammar (numbered feature sections each carrying a rendered product-UI figure).
4. Full route sweep: /, /architecture, /features, /compare, /security, /roadmap, /faq, /blog, /agent-guide.md, /how-it-works, plus docs.
5. Docs: task-oriented walkthrough guides (numbered steps, runnable command, expected output, failure mode) and enriched generated tool pages.
6. Marketing copy moves from abstract metaphor to concrete, second-person, proof-bearing claims.

Evidence required: build green, lint green, every nav destination returns 200.
